skill.name: threejs-shaders
skill.description: Custom GLSL vertex and fragment shaders: uniforms, varyings, shader chunks, extending built-in materials, instanced attributes, plus the same effects as node materials with TSL on WebGPU. Use when writing a shader, a custom material or effect, moving vertices in a shader, or porting GLSL to TSL.
skill.summary: Guidance for Three.js r186 shader effects using GLSL, custom materials, and portable TSL node materials.
skill.author: cloudai-x

security_audit.summary: All 118 static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, JavaScript shader strings, GLSL entry points, and shader chunk keys. The reviewed documentation contains rendering examples and relative texture loads, with no evidence of shell execution, credential access, reconnaissance, or prompt injection. No evidence found of malicious intent or additional semantic security risks.

content.user_title: Build Three.js Shaders with GLSL and TSL
content.value_statement: Custom Three.js effects require careful handling of shader inputs, color conversion, and renderer compatibility. This skill provides GLSL and TSL examples for building effects and diagnosing common material errors.
actual_capabilities: Explain ShaderMaterial and RawShaderMaterial setup, GLSL declarations, uniforms, varyings, and output color conversion.
Provide examples for vertex displacement, Fresnel shading, dissolve effects, and instanced attributes.
Show how to extend built-in WebGL materials with onBeforeCompile and distinct program cache keys.
Explain shader chunk reuse, compile error logging, and visual debugging of UVs and normals.
Demonstrate TSL node materials, reusable functions, time nodes, texture sampling, and GLSL migration for WebGPURenderer.
Identify common Three.js r186 shader API mistakes and renderer compatibility problems.
limitations: Targets Three.js r186; other releases can require different APIs and shader chunks.
Provides documentation and examples, not a packaged renderer, automated shader compiler, or test suite.
Requires a Three.js project and a compatible browser or GPU environment to run and verify examples.
References texture files and related skills that are not included in this single-file skill.

use_cases.title: Add Animated Product Materials
use_cases.description: Create color waves, displacement, or Fresnel effects while keeping shader uniforms and color conversion consistent.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers building interactive product viewers

use_cases.title: Prototype Game Visual Effects
use_cases.description: Adapt dissolve shaders and custom instanced attributes for scene objects, then inspect shader errors and coordinate spaces.
use_cases.target_user: Technical artists prototyping browser game effects

use_cases.title: Migrate Effects to TSL
use_cases.description: Translate GLSL effects into node materials and reusable TSL functions for WebGPURenderer with its WebGL 2 fallback.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Shader
prompt_templates.prompt: Use threejs-shaders to create an animated color wave on a plane in Three.js r186 with WebGLRenderer. Include time uniforms and output color conversion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: build a minimal ShaderMaterial effect.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Material Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Three.js r186 shader: [paste shader and renderer setup]. Diagnose dark colors, missing uniform declarations, and coordinate-space mismatches. Explain the required corrections.

prompt_templates.title: Extend a Lit Material
prompt_templates.prompt: Add animated vertex displacement to my r186 MeshStandardMaterial with onBeforeCompile: [paste material setup]. Preserve lighting and use distinct program cache keys for shader variants.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: customize built-in WebGL material shaders.

prompt_templates.title: Port a Dissolve Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: Port this GLSL dissolve effect to a reusable TSL Fn for Three.js r186: [paste shader]. Use WebGPURenderer, updatable progress, and portable texture sampling. Identify backend-specific assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: migrate an effect to portable node materials.

output_examples.input: My ShaderMaterial renders darker than a built-in material with the same color.
output: Color uniforms created with THREE.Color hold linear values.
Apply the tone mapping and color space chunks after writing the fragment color.
Check the render target and output pass before adding another color conversion.

output_examples.input: My custom ShaderMaterial stops working after switching to WebGPURenderer.
output: ShaderMaterial and onBeforeCompile belong to the WebGLRenderer workflow.
Use MeshBasicNodeMaterial for an unlit effect or MeshStandardNodeMaterial for a lit effect.
Rewrite the effect using TSL nodes and reusable functions instead of passing GLSL shader strings.

output_examples.input: All instances overlap when I use my own vertex shader.
output: Declaring an InstancedMesh does not apply its instance transforms inside a custom shader.
Apply instanceMatrix before the model-view and projection transforms.
Custom offset attributes also require bounds that account for the displacement.

best_practices: Check the installed Three.js release and renderer backend before choosing GLSL shaders or TSL node materials.
Keep lighting vectors in one coordinate space and verify texture color spaces before adjusting shader colors.
Inspect compiled shader errors and visualize intermediate values before adding more effect logic.
anti_patterns: Use ShaderMaterial or onBeforeCompile under WebGPURenderer instead of selecting node materials.
Mix world-space camera directions with view-space normals when calculating Fresnel or rim lighting.
Copy obsolete shader chunk names or TSL imports without checking the targeted release.

faq.question: Which Three.js version does this skill target?
faq.answer: The documentation targets Three.js r186. Check APIs and shader chunk names when using another release.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill provides Markdown guidance and examples for these assistants, rather than a separate executable tool.

faq.question: Does ShaderMaterial work with WebGPURenderer?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs WebGPURenderer users to TSL node materials instead of ShaderMaterial, RawShaderMaterial, or onBeforeCompile.

faq.question: Can it help migrate GLSL effects to TSL?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains node material slots, reusable functions, uniforms, texture sampling, and backend-specific GLSL or WGSL limitations.

faq.question: Does the skill include textures or a runnable application?
faq.answer: No. It contains one documentation file. You must provide a Three.js project and any referenced texture assets.

faq.question: Does it automatically test shader correctness or performance?
faq.answer: No. It explains compile error inspection and visual debugging, but you must run and test effects in your target environment.
